title: Anchor prod held 50 min and dev leaked an admin user: gate flows failed on TCP resets the gate never reruns
summary: Seven Anchor PRs merged within 22 s at 20:34Z, and three of the four Anchor post-deploy gates that followed failed on `connection reset by peer` from the Cloudflare edge before any response. The gate reruns nothing, so each reset turned the gate red and held Anchor prod until a human reran the failed job at 21:44Z. Three reset requests were cleanup or create writes: a dev product, a platform invitation and an ADMIN platform user stayed behind, the user because its `register` POST was applied while the response was lost. The 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-23 fixes (rerun once, report leaks) only ever lived in the routine's `run_suites.sh`. The gate workflow now reruns transport-only failures once and prints `TRANSPORT-LEAK`, and the leaked data is deleted. Why the edge resets these connections is still open.

impact.text: Dev and CI only. Anchor prod promotion of the security fixes #326-#331 waited about 50 min (no customer impact: prod kept the previous release). Three dev resources leaked for about 3 h, one of them an ADMIN platform user of the dev tenant.

trigger: A pooled HTTPS connection from the gate runner (1340p, 192.168.2.18) to the Cloudflare edge `172.64.80.1` was reset while six requests of `anchor: invitations` used it, right after the flow's 61 s `wait-x-expiry` delay.
detection: The gate failed and the `alert-deploy-failure` job ran at 20:58:05Z. Nobody connected the three red gates to transport: the routine found them at 2026-11-06T00:08Z while reading gate results, and found the leaks only by reading each failed execution's `always` nodes. The gate reports no leak.
resolution: A human reran the failed job of run 42114438354 at 21:44Z (green), which promoted Anchor to prod. On 2026-11-06 the routine deleted the leaked product, invitation and ADMIN platform user with a temporary flow, and shipped a rerun-once + leak report step in the gate workflow.

events.label: Seven Anchor PRs merge within 22 s (#326-#331)
6 invitations nodes reset after a 61 s delay
events.detail: `accept-x`, `get-x`, `lookup-x`, `update-x`, `search-x-*` all fail at the same second: `read tcp 192.168.2.18:39388->172.64.80.1:443: read: connection reset by peer`.

events.label: Gate red, deploy-failure alert job runs, prod held
Gate 42111072987: 3 writes reset, 3 resources leak
events.detail: `platform-invitation` cleanup DELETE, `platform-users` register POST (applied: ADMIN user created) and `resource-permission` cleanup-product DELETE, all on connections to `172.64.80.1`.

events.label: Gate 42114438354 a1: 3 more flows reset
events.detail: Same second, the runner's own progress POSTs to `api.echopoint.dev` also reset: host-side path to the edge, not Anchor.

events.label: Human reruns the failed gate job: green
Routine suite: same invitations reset from the laptop
events.detail: Direct LAN this time (192.168.2.50), no VPN. `run_suites.sh` reran it green. A plain HTTP/1.1 reuse after 65 s idle did not reproduce.

events.label: Leaked product, invitation and ADMIN user deleted

whys.problem: Anchor prod waited ~50 min for its security fixes and dev kept a leaked ADMIN user after gate flows hit TCP resets

because.text: Gate flows failed when a reused connection to the Cloudflare edge was reset before any response
because.evidence: Gate logs of runs 42107762222, 42111072987, 42114438354: `read: connection reset by peer` to `172.64.80.1:443`

because.text: The runner fails a POST, PUT or DELETE at once on a reset pooled connection: Go replays only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE
because.evidence: `net/http` `shouldRetryRequest`; every failed node was a write or ran in a burst with one

because.text: The runner has no replay or health-check policy for pooled connections before a response byte (open since 2026-10-21)
Why the path to the edge resets these connections: laptop (VPN and LAN) and 1340p both see it; HTTP/1.1 reuse after 65 s did not
because.evidence: 6 invitations nodes reset right after a 61 s delay in the gate and locally; `idle.py` probe 30/55/65 s all 200

because.text: A transient reset turned the promotion gate red three times
The rerun-once fix of 2026-10-21 lives only in the routine's `run_suites.sh`, not in the gate workflow
because.evidence: `ci-workflows/.github/workflows/echopoint-test.yml` before this fix: one action step, no rerun

because.text: Transport handling was added to one caller of the suite instead of the shared gate workflow every caller uses
A reset write left data behind that no cleanup could reach
The register POST was applied while its response was lost, so `me` never ran and the always `delete-user` was skipped
because.evidence: Platform user search for the run's garbage address found `puser_3Lhk0OBU…` (ADMIN) at 00:20Z

because.text: Cleanups read ids from the create's response, so a write whose response is lost owns data nothing can find, and the gate reports no leak

contributing: Seven PRs merged in 22 s produced seven serial deploy+gate runs in 45 min on the host that also runs dev, so one reset class had seven chances.
The gate runs with `parallel: 3` on one runner process, so one reset connection failed requests of two flows at once (21:17:42Z, local port 48512).

well: The rerun of one failed job was enough to promote: nothing in the code was wrong.
Each execution keeps its node results, so the leaks could be found and deleted hours later.
wrong: A fix verified on the laptop was marked `verified` while the gate, the caller that holds prod, had no copy of it.
A skipped `always` cleanup was treated as harmless; a write applied with a lost response makes it a leak.
lucky: The leaked ADMIN user sat in the dev tenant; the same flow against a shared tenant would leave an admin account behind.
No security fix was urgent for prod during the 50 min hold.
A human happened to rerun the job; the routine does not rerun gates.

actions.what: Gate workflow reruns a flow whose failure is a transport error once, fails on more than 5, and prints `TRANSPORT-LEAK` for each uncompleted `always` request node
`anchor: platform-users` cleanup finds the registered user by its unique email instead of the register response
flow-suite-testing skill: a create whose response can be lost is cleaned up by a lookup on a unique key
Runner: replay PUT/DELETE before any response byte and health-check idle pooled HTTP/2 connections (ping or a shorter idle timeout); decide the customer-facing policy
Find why the path to `172.64.80.1` resets connections (HTTP/2 idle, edge timeout) with an HTTP/2 reuse probe after 61 s from 1340p

messaging.internal: Anchor gates went red 3 times on 2026-11-05 on TCP resets to Cloudflare, not on code. The gate now reruns transport-only failures once and reports leaked cleanups. Leaked dev data is deleted.
